functional.title: Tenant, site, and asset registry
functional.definition: Authorized users can register tenants, sites, refrigeration assets, sensors, asset model and serial identifiers, warranty data, approved vendors, service history, and food-at-risk values with versioned provenance.

functional.title: Telemetry ingestion and freshness
functional.definition: The system ingests authenticated temperature, power, current, door, and heartbeat readings, pins each sample to immutable effective-dated device-to-asset assignment and channel/calibration revisions, preserves device sequence and source time, and derives explicit fresh, stale, offline, or invalid status.

functional.title: Incident creation and deduplication
functional.definition: Policy-qualified telemetry or an authorized manual report opens one incident per asset and fault window, links corroborating signals, and prevents duplicate active incidents.

functional.title: Evidence-based incident triage
functional.definition: The incident engine classifies urgency, pins the active versioned tenant procedure and computed response or containment deadline at incident opening, records any authorized deadline amendment without rewriting the original, assigns durable ownership, identifies likely fault family, required evidence and allowed next actions, and labels any optional food-risk estimate as non-authoritative with provenance and uncertainty.

functional.title: Manual, BOM, and history retrieval
functional.definition: The evidence service retrieves the exact asset revision's manuals, parts lists, warranty terms, prior work orders, and approved-vendor records, returning page- or record-level citations and conflicts.

functional.title: Deterministic compatibility decision
functional.definition: A deterministic policy evaluates exact OEM or manufacturer part number, asset revision, electrical and mechanical constraints, certification, warranty, and named-engineer approvals to return ALLOW, HOLD, or REJECT.

functional.title: Provider and catalog discovery
functional.definition: The system discovers eligible technicians, suppliers, diagnostic services, temporary-containment products, and catalog offers through auditable adapters without treating search rank as approval.

functional.title: Quote and contact orchestration
functional.definition: The system can prepare and track quote, availability, arrival-estimate, and diagnostic-commitment contacts through phone, email, and structured provider APIs with consent, transcript provenance, and idempotency; unpaid execution stays in the provider module, while every paid contact becomes a bounded commercial intent executed and reconciled only by the exclusive broker.

functional.title: Cost-to-recovery planning
functional.definition: The planner ranks only policy-eligible recovery plans using repair cost, delay multiplied by downtime cost, a versioned tenant risk estimate multiplied by inventory value, and repeat-failure risk, exposes every input and configured containment deadline, and holds rather than ranks when mandatory inputs are missing.

functional.title: Approval and escalation policy
functional.definition: The policy layer determines whether a proposed action is automatically permitted, requires a named human or engineer approval, or must be rejected, based on safety class, substitution, amount, evidence, and site policy.

functional.title: Bounded Kite spending session
functional.definition: An authorized operator can create a purpose-, incident-, merchant-, action-, amount-, time-, and currency-bounded Kite Passport spending session whose effective limits are displayed before approval.

functional.title: Paid-action broker and reconciliation
functional.definition: A single exclusive broker executes authorized Kite-paid calls and purchases with pre-generated client operation and idempotency keys, immutable intent and attempt records, receipts, UNKNOWN outcome handling, and authoritative lookup or proven same-key replay before retry.

functional.title: Order and service-job lifecycle
functional.definition: The system tracks purchase, shipment, cancellation, substitution, appointment, technician arrival, work status, and provider failure as explicit states tied to the approved recovery plan.

functional.title: Recovery evidence ingestion
functional.definition: The system ingests post-intervention telemetry, installed-part barcode or serial, technician records, CMMS signatures, and authorized-operator attestations with source identity and time.

functional.title: Authoritative recovery verification
functional.definition: An incident closes only when a stable telemetry window beginning after the bound authorized intervention milestone uses fresh non-backfilled samples from the pinned asset and sensor revisions, and required installed-part identity plus CMMS or authorized-operator evidence satisfy deterministic recovery policy.

functional.title: Escalation and reopening
functional.definition: Provider timeout, failed intervention, incompatible substitution, repeated fault, disputed evidence, or lost recovery signal reopens or escalates the incident without discarding prior evidence.

functional.title: CMMS and work-order integration
functional.definition: The system reads and writes work-order status, evidence references, approved plan, costs, receipts, installed-part identity, and closeout decision through isolated, replay-safe CMMS adapters.

functional.title: Evidence ledger and export
functional.definition: Every material input, model proposal, policy decision, approval, external action, payment state, receipt, and recovery decision is recorded in an append-only, exportable evidence ledger with correlation identifiers.

functional.title: Operations user interface
functional.definition: The web application provides accessible, responsive views for fleet health, incident timeline, evidence, compatibility, plan comparison, approvals, spend, fulfillment, recovery proof, audit, and administration.

functional.title: Actionable notifications
functional.definition: The system sends role-appropriate notifications for critical incidents, evidence gaps, approvals, spend exceptions, provider changes, recovery, and reopen events with direct context and recovery paths.

functional.title: Policy administration
functional.definition: Authorized administrators can version safety classes, thresholds, recovery windows, approved vendors, amount limits, escalation routes, retention, and integration settings with effective dates and audit history.

functional.title: Real-input pilot and demo mode
functional.definition: A pilot can use an authenticated physical sensor or explicitly labeled deployed edge simulator, real manuals, real provider responses, and at least one real bounded Kite-paid action while clearly labeling any unavailable external outcome.

functional.title: Privacy and data lifecycle
functional.definition: The system supports data minimization, purpose limitation, configurable retention, legal hold, export, redaction, deletion workflows, and tenant-scoped handling for operational and communication data.

functional.title: Authentication, RBAC, and tenant isolation
functional.definition: Human, device, service, and integration identities authenticate separately; permissions enforce tenant, site, role, action, approval, and credential boundaries on every read and write.

nonfunctional.title: Reproducible build
nonfunctional.definition: A clean supported environment can install, validate, test, build, migrate, seed, and start the product through documented pinned commands and a committed lockfile.

nonfunctional.title: Restart-safe reliability
nonfunctional.definition: Durable state, jobs, outbox records, and reconciliation allow safe restart without losing incidents, approvals, payment outcomes, orders, or recovery evidence.

nonfunctional.title: Idempotency and concurrency
nonfunctional.definition: All external commands and state transitions are idempotent, concurrency-controlled, and safe under duplicate delivery, timeout, retry, and multi-worker execution.

nonfunctional.title: Bounded resource use
nonfunctional.definition: Ingestion, retrieval, model, provider, notification, and reconciliation work has explicit concurrency, size, rate, retry, timeout, and cost bounds with backpressure.

nonfunctional.title: Least-privilege security
nonfunctional.definition: Services, users, devices, adapters, and agents receive only required capabilities; sensitive actions require explicit policy and credential isolation; secure defaults fail closed.

nonfunctional.title: Privacy by design
nonfunctional.definition: Sensitive operational, personal, transcript, and payment data is minimized, encrypted in transit and at rest where supported, redacted from logs, and governed by retention policy.

nonfunctional.title: Accessible interaction
nonfunctional.definition: The user interface targets WCAG 2.2 AA, full keyboard operation, visible focus, semantic labels, non-color-only status, reduced motion, and screen-reader-readable critical decisions.

nonfunctional.title: Operational performance
nonfunctional.definition: The product defines and measures latency and availability objectives for telemetry freshness, incident opening, policy evaluation, UI response, notification, and reconciliation without hiding degraded state.

nonfunctional.title: Observability and auditability
nonfunctional.definition: Structured logs, metrics, traces, audit events, health checks, and correlation identifiers expose every critical path while preventing secrets and unnecessary personal data from entering telemetry.

nonfunctional.title: Bounded AI with provenance
nonfunctional.definition: Model inputs, outputs, citations, versions, confidence, and policy disposition are recorded; structured validation, tool limits, and deterministic gates prevent model text from directly causing unsafe or paid actions.

nonfunctional.title: Adapter portability
nonfunctional.definition: Sensor, model, Kite, provider, merchant, messaging, and CMMS integrations sit behind contract-tested adapters so unavailable vendors degrade explicitly rather than corrupting the core domain.

nonfunctional.title: Traceable delivery
nonfunctional.definition: Each implementation change maps to requirement, invariant, module, and test identifiers and produces reviewable commands, results, evidence, migration notes, and rollback notes.

invariants.title: Authoritative recovery proof
invariants.definition: A provider, model, purchase receipt, or human assertion alone can never prove recovery; closure requires the incident's configured independent telemetry window plus every mandatory identity and authorization signal.

invariants.title: No model authorization
invariants.definition: An LLM may extract, summarize, rank, and propose, but it can never independently approve compatibility, substitution, safety-critical work, spending, or incident closure.

invariants.title: Revision-bound decisions
invariants.definition: Every compatibility, approval, purchase, installation, and recovery decision is bound to an immutable tenant and incident, asset identity revision including model and serial, evidence revision, policy revision, and proposed-action digest.

invariants.title: Compatibility fails closed
invariants.definition: Missing, ambiguous, conflicting, stale, or non-exact compatibility evidence produces HOLD or REJECT; semantic similarity, seller text, and search rank never produce ALLOW.

invariants.title: Hard spending bounds
invariants.definition: No paid action may exceed the effective incident, action, merchant, amount, currency, purpose, or expiry bounds approved by an authorized operator, and every reservation, capture, release, refund, reversal, or explicit authority adjustment must preserve the append-only gross-cap and net-settlement conservation equations.

invariants.title: Exclusive credential and egress broker
invariants.definition: Only the payment broker may hold Kite credentials or reach paid Kite endpoints; reasoning agents, browsers, UI clients, and other workers receive neither raw credentials nor bypass egress.

invariants.title: Payment intent idempotency
invariants.definition: One canonical action digest plus immutable execution-authority identity maps to at most one economic intent; duplicates return it, and a successor under fresh authority is allowed only after every prior intent for that action is terminal with definite proof of no effect.

invariants.title: Unknown is not failure
invariants.definition: A timeout, disconnect, or ambiguous external response becomes UNKNOWN and must be reconciled through a pre-existing client operation key against authoritative provider state or proven same-key replay before retry, refund, replacement, or failure is declared; an adapter without that capability cannot retry autonomously.

invariants.title: Single active incident window
invariants.definition: For a tenant, site, asset, and configured fault window, concurrent triggers converge on one active incident and append evidence rather than opening independent recovery spend paths.

invariants.title: Append-only evidence lineage
invariants.definition: Material evidence and decision records are immutable; corrections create linked revisions, and historical decisions remain reproducible from the revisions that governed them.

invariants.title: Stale data never appears healthy
invariants.definition: Stale, missing, delayed, invalid, or unauthenticated telemetry can never render a green healthy or recovered state and must expose its freshness condition.

invariants.title: External outcome honesty
invariants.definition: The product separately distinguishes REQUESTED, ACCEPTED, CONFIRMED, UNKNOWN, FAILED, and CANCELLED external outcomes from ELIGIBLE or UNSUPPORTED adapter capability, and never presents a request, local simulation, or payment receipt as fulfilled work.

invariants.title: Secret non-disclosure
invariants.definition: Secrets, raw Kite credentials, payment authorization material, and access tokens never enter model prompts, client bundles, logs, traces, exports, or repository history. Private communication content may enter an approved model run only as a purpose-limited, minimum redacted excerpt under tenant policy with consent where required, and may be displayed or exported only to authorized roles with retention and redaction controls.

invariants.title: No premature completion or release
invariants.definition: An order, provider-completed flag, receipt, installed-part claim, or transient safe reading cannot close the incident or release completion-dependent value before the full recovery policy passes.

invariants.title: Human approval for high-risk change
invariants.definition: Every substitute part, non-exact match, safety-critical intervention, policy override, or approval outside pre-authorized bounds requires a named authorized human or engineer and creates a signed audit record.

invariants.title: Tenant isolation
invariants.definition: No identity, query, cache, job, object, event, export, adapter, or observability path may read, infer, mutate, or act on another tenant's data or authority.
